cctv: Every camera needs a cable run back to the recorder. Outdoor runs want proper external cable.
Analogue cameras need a 12V power supply; IP cameras are powered by the recorder's PoE ports.
A small UPS on the recorder keeps the cameras recording when the power goes.
wifi_ap: Most access points are powered by the network cable — check the switch supplies PoE, or add an injector.
An access point goes where the coverage is needed, which usually means a cable run.
Wi-Fi through load-shedding means the switch and the router stay powered too.
netgear: Every port needs a lead, and the right length keeps a cabinet tidy.
Rack gear needs a rack; a cabinet keeps it out of the way and out of reach.
Keep it up in an outage
A switch that drops takes the whole network with it.
laptops: Sized to the screen, not to the brand.
The single cheapest thing that makes a laptop feel like a desk.
One cable to screen, keyboard, network and power.
desktop: A screen to go with it
Check what is in the box before buying twice.
A tower does not enjoy a hard shutdown.
printers: Match them to the printer model, not the brand — the numbers matter.
We are IT distributors; paper costs more to freight than to buy down the road.
monitors: Check what the machine actually has before assuming HDMI.
A stand or arm buys back desk space.
mesh: Mesh extends a network; it does not replace the router unless it says so.

Mesh nodes are useless if the fibre box is dark.
